title: No More Brain Fog: New AI Architecture Cuts Memory Bloat by 54%!
summary: Researchers have introduced the FOCUS framework (arXiv:2609.37590) featuring Anchored Iterative Summarization to solve cognitive context drift in long-horizon LLM agents. The architecture slashes peak memory token usage by up to 54% while maintaining task execution accuracy above 95%, resolving the root cause of 65% of enterprise AI failures.
raw_text: So check this out: if you've ever watched an autonomous AI agent attempt a complex multi-step coding task, you know they usually lose their minds after 20 minutes. It turns out that sprawling context windows don't actually solve the problem—nearly 65% of enterprise agent failures happen simply because models get hopelessly confused by their own massive, uncompressed chat histories. But a brilliant new arXiv paper just dropped introducing FOCUS, and it completely fixes agent memory drift. Instead of relying on crude full-history LLM summaries that hallucinate and erase technical details, FOCUS uses 'Anchored Iterative Summarization.' It locks in a permanent anchor tracking original user intent, decisions made, and pending actions, while compressing only the latest interactions. Paired with an automated optimization supervisor called ACON, this framework cuts peak memory token usage by up to 54% while keeping operational accuracy above 95%! In my opinion, this is the exact plumbing breakthrough developers desperately needed to finally build reliable, persistent AI agents that can work for days without breaking.

title: Jailbreak Immunity: New 'Skilder' Protocol Locks Down Rogue AI Tools!
summary: The newly published Skilder framework (arXiv:2609.28693) introduces Progressive Skill Discovery to enforce strict, role-scoped access control on autonomous LLM agents via Model Context Protocol servers. By dynamically gating API tool awareness behind verified roles, the protocol prevents prompt injection exploits from executing unauthorized enterprise commands.
raw_text: Here's the wild part about building autonomous agents: if you hand an LLM an API tool list, any clever prompt injection attack can trick it into wiping your production database. But an awesome new arXiv research paper just introduced 'Skilder,' and it's basically the ultimate bouncer for agentic AI. Instead of dumping every single API tool directly into the agent's system prompt where hackers can manipulate it, Skilder uses 'Progressive Skill Discovery.' The agent initializes knowing only broad role definitions, not the actual execution tools. To run a command, it has to dynamically authenticate and discover capabilities through a centralized Model Context Protocol server that strictly enforces least-privilege security boundaries. If an agent assigned to a basic customer support role suddenly tries to run a destructive database command, Skilder's router deterministically blocks the execution at the architectural layer. Natural language tricks won't save the hacker. Honestly, this is huge for the industry because hard deterministic boundaries like Skilder are the only way enterprises will ever trust AI agents with live infrastructure.
